plan.title: Liver 3-group DESeq2 LRT/Wald + ORA vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 liver samples, 3 groups of 4 (control, treated_a, treated_b), unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples; metadata.csv gives condition per sample). The question has two parts: (1) which genes differ across all three groups at all -> answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (LRT) of the full model ~condition against the reduced model ~1, which is the correct 'any difference among >=3 groups' test since a single Wald coefficient cannot span a 3-level factor; (2) which genes does each treatment change vs control -> answered by two pairwise DESeq2 Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) with control set as the explicit reference level, followed by ashr shrinkage of each contrast's log2FC (ashr, not apeglm, because a non-reference-level contrast is not a single model coefficient). Sample structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) runs first to catch outliers/batch structure before any test. Multiple testing uses BH within each contrast (LRT contrast and each Wald contrast separately), independent filtering on, alpha=0.05, with a p-value-histogram diagnostic. Because the design has no covariates and is unbatched, the DESeq2 GLM design is simply ~condition; import is directly from the gene-level count matrix (no tximport intermediate exists in the delivered files, so this step works on the gene x sample counts.csv directly, treating it as the DESeq2 dds input matrix). Downstream, gene identifiers are mapped to Entrez with org.Hs.eg.db, and functional interpretation of each of the two treatment-vs-control gene lists and the any-group significant list uses over-representation analysis (ORA, per the knowledge-service ruling for this situation, since the question frames itself around discrete DE gene lists rather than requesting a ranked enrichment) against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways-human, and GO Biological Process, all with the tested genes as the universe and a 15-500 gene-set size window; if a contrast yields fewer than ~50 significant genes, ORA is reported as underpowered and flagged rather than over-interpreted. All steps report package versions, thresholds, and design/contrast definitions explicitly, per the grounded procedure returned by the domain knowledge service for a 3-group unbatched design with 4 replicates per group.

steps.method: keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (4)
design ~ condition, reference level = control, gene-level count matrix from Salmon (no tximport/txi available - counts.csv already gene-level)
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (full ~condition vs reduced ~1) for any-group difference, then Wald contrasts treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control
ashr shrinkage on each Wald contrast
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast, alpha=0.05, independent filtering on
fgsea preranked on Wald stat, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways human, per contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways human, run once per contrast (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) on the full ranked gene list

clusterProfiler enrichGO (BP) with universe = tested genes, on significant DE gene list per contrast; complemented by ORA against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome and WikiPathways human gene sets via clusterProfiler enricher; report the significant-gene-list size and skip if under ~50 genes
